newsitem.title: ITALY: GTE quits consortium for Italy PCN licence.
newsitem.headline: GTE quits consortium for Italy PCN licence.

text.p: U.S. telephone company GTE has left a consortium preparing to compete for Italy's third mobile phone licence which includes Italian private broadcaster Mediaset, a Mediaset adviser said on Wednesday.

Elserino Piol, Mediaset telecoms adviser, said on the fringe of a news conference too many delays and lack of regulation had pushed GTE to leave the consortium which was formed to compete for the PCN standard mobile phone licence.
The Italian government has not yet tendered the licence and Piol said repeated postponements of the tender had prompted GTE's departure.

Norway's Telenor, British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) remain in the consortium along with Mediaset, the broadcasting and advertising arm of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's media empire.
Mediaset sources said despite GTE's exit the consortium would continue its research for eventual participation in the licence tender.
Berlusconi said recently he knew for certain Mediaset did not intend to partecipate in the tender for the third licence but this was later denied by Mediaset chairman Fedele Confalonieri.
Confalonieri said Mediaset intended to take part "but we are concerned because every day that passes strengthens those who are in the sector already."
Mediaset has said that if the tender is not opened within the year its interest could vanish.
